humbles itself, thus it can be superior;
impairs itself, thus it is truly firm;
accepts incompleteness, thus it is fully complete;
dwells in turbidity and disgrace, thus it is fresh;
sees insufficiency, thus it can be worthy.
The Way does nothing, yet nothing is left undone.
Lǎozi said:
All who learn,
if they can understand the distinction between Heaven and humanity,
comprehend the root of order and chaos,
purify their hearts and clarify their intentions to preserve it,
will see its beginning and end.
Returning to emptiness and non-being,
they may be called enlightened.
The root of governance
is benevolence and righteousness,
while its branches
are laws and regulations.
What gives life to people
is the root,
what does not give life
is the branches;
root and branches
are one body,
loving both
is human nature;
putting the root before the branches
is called the noble person,
putting the branches before the root
is called the petty person.
Laws are created
to assist righteousness;
emphasizing laws while discarding righteousness
is like valuing one's hat and shoes while forgetting one's head and feet.
Benevolence and righteousness
are broad and lofty;
to expand their breadth without increasing their substance leads to ruin,
to heighten them without broadening their foundation leads to collapse.
Therefore, without enlarging the beam,
it cannot bear heavy loads;
nothing bears weight like a beam,
nothing bears a state like virtue.
The ruler's possession of the people
is like a city having foundations,
or a tree having roots;
deep roots mean firm foundations,
thick foundations mean stability above.
Thus, affairs not rooted in the Way and virtue
cannot serve as guiding principles;
words not in accord with ancient kings
cannot be considered the Way;
opportunistic picking and choosing,
techniques of single actions or temporary achievements
are not the universal Way of the world.
Lǎozi said:
The way of governing people
is like Zàofǔ driving a team of four horses;
he harmonizes them with reins and bits,
regulates them through his chest and heart,
internally attaining it in his center,
externally matching the horses' will,
thus able to take the road and reach far,
with energy to spare,
advancing, retreating, turning and curving,
all as desired -
truly he has mastered the art.
Now authority and power
are the ruler's chariot,
and great ministers
are the ruler's team of horses;
he cannot leave the safety of the chariot,
nor lose control of the horses' hearts with his hands.
Thus if the horses are not coordinated,
even Zàofǔ cannot take the road;
if ruler and ministers are not harmonious,
even a sage cannot bring order.
Hold the Way to guide them,
and average talents can be fully utilized;
clarify distinctions to show them,
and wickedness can be stopped;
when things come, observe their changes,
when affairs arise, respond to their transformations -
if those nearby are not disordered, those far away will be ordered.
Not using forced methods,
but attaining the natural Way,
ten thousand actions will not fail.
Lǎozi said:
All who follow the Way
block evil paths,
prevent what has not yet happened,
not valuing self-approval,
but valuing making wrongdoing impossible.
Therefore it is said: Do not create desires,
and there will be no daily craving;
do not create things worth seizing,
and there will be no daily contention.
Thus human desires are released,
and public justice prevails.
Those with excess are restrained within measure,
those with insufficiency reach adequacy -
thus the world can be unified.
If one abandons duties to listen to praise and blame,
discards merit to employ factions,
then unusual talents will flee,
and officials will not advance in their posts;
customs will be disordered in the state,
meritorious ministers will contend at court.
Therefore, having the Way to guide people,
without the Way one is controlled by others.
Lǎozi said:
Governing a state has constants, with benefiting the people as fundamental;
government and teaching have principles, with effective commands as primary.
If it benefits the people,
it need not imitate antiquity;
if it suits affairs,
it need not follow customs.
Therefore sages adapt laws to changing times,
and adjust rituals to evolving customs;
clothing and tools
should each be suitable for their use;
laws, regulations and commands
should each be appropriate to their circumstances.
Thus changing antiquity should not be condemned,
and following customs should not be excessively praised.
Reciting the books of ancient kings
is not as good as hearing their words;
hearing their words
is not as good as understanding why they spoke;
understanding why they spoke
means understanding what cannot be spoken.
Therefore
"The Way that can be spoken
is not the eternal Way;
the name that can be named
is not the eternal name."
Thus what the sage follows is called the Way,
like metal and stone -
once tuned cannot be changed;
affairs are like zithers -
when the tune ends, change the melody.
Legal systems, rituals and music
are tools of governance,
not the means of governing itself.
Therefore one cannot discuss the ultimate Way with narrow scholars -
they are confused by customs and bound by teachings.
Lǎozi said:
How can the world have constant laws!
What fits contemporary affairs,
accords with human principles,
follows Heaven and Earth,
and is careful regarding spirits -
this can bring correct governance.
In ancient times, the Three Sovereigns had no commands yet people followed;
the Five Emperors had commands but no punishments;
the Xià people did not break promises,
the Shāng people swore oaths,
the Zhōu people made covenants.
In the decline of latter ages,
people endure shame and轻视侮辱,
covet gain and lack shame.
Therefore laws, regulations and commands
assess customs and regulate urgency;
tools and instruments
adapt to changing times for appropriate use.
Those constrained by laws
cannot accomplish great deeds;
those bound by ritual
cannot respond to change.
One must have unique vision's clarity,
unique hearing's acuity,
then can master the Way and act.
Those who know the source of laws
can adapt to the times and change;
those who don't know governance's source
will eventually create chaos despite following rules;
today's learners
follow precedents and inherit traditions,
grasping texts,
guarding written rules,
thinking this brings order -
like fitting a square peg in a round hole,
achieving proper fit is difficult indeed.
Preserving endangered states and ordering chaos -
even the wise may fail;
praising the Way and citing antiquity -
even fools can do in excess.
Therefore unused laws
sages do not implement;
unverified words
enlightened rulers do not heed.
Wénzǐ asked:
"From where does law arise?"
Lǎozǐ said:
"Law arises from righteousness,
righteousness arises from what suits the multitude,
and what suits the multitude accords with human hearts.
This is the essence of governance.
Law does not descend from heaven,
nor does it emerge from earth,
but springs from human society,
reflecting back to rectify oneself.
Truly understanding its root,
one will not be confused by its branches;
knowing its essence,
one will not be perplexed by doubts.
What one demands of oneself,
one does not criticize in others;
what one lacks in oneself,
one does not demand of others.
What is established for subordinates should not be abolished by superiors,
what is prohibited for the people should not be practiced by the ruler.
Therefore, when a ruler establishes laws,
he uses them as standards for himself,
so when prohibitions are upheld by his own person,
then orders will be implemented among the people.
Now law is
the plumb line of the world,
the measure of the ruler.
To promulgate laws
is to legalize what is unlawful.
After laws are established,
those who meet the standard are rewarded,
those who deviate are punished.
Even the noble and honored are not lightly rewarded,
the lowly and humble are not heavily punished.
Those who violate the law,
though virtuous, must be punished;
those who conform to the standard,
though unworthy, are without guilt.
Thus public justice prevails,
and private desires are blocked.
In ancient times, officials were appointed
to restrain the people from acting wantonly;
rulers were established
to control officials from acting arbitrarily;
laws, regulations, and methods
were created to restrain rulers from ruling autocratically.
When no one can act wantonly,
then the Way prevails and principle is realized,
thus returning to non-action.
Non-action
does not mean not moving,
but that nothing proceeds from selfish intention.
Lǎozǐ said:
"Those skilled in rewarding
expend little yet encourage much;
those skilled in punishing
use few penalties yet stop wrongdoing;
those skilled in giving
use little yet accomplish much virtue;
those skilled in taking
receive much yet incur no resentment.
Therefore, the sage follows what people like to encourage goodness,
and follows what people hate to prohibit wrongdoing.
Reward one person and the world follows;
punish one person and the world fears.
Thus the ultimate reward costs nothing,
the ultimate punishment is not excessive.
The sage maintains simplicity yet governs broadly -
this is what it means."
Lǎozǐ said:
"The way of ministers
is to discuss what is right and act appropriately,
to initiate affairs and take the lead,
to preserve their duties and clarify their roles,
thereby achieving success.
Thus when ruler and minister follow different ways, there is order;
when they follow the same way, there is chaos.
Each attaining what is suitable,
acting appropriately,
then superior and inferior have means to employ each other.
Therefore, branches should not be larger than the trunk,
the tips should not be stronger than the root,
meaning light and heavy, small and large have means to control each other.
Those who obtain authority
hold very little,
yet control very much;
preserve very simply,
yet govern very broadly.
A tree ten arm-spans around
supports a roof of thousand jun weight -
this is due to its position;
a five-inch latch
can control opening and closing -
this is due to its crucial location.
Issuing commands that must be followed,
where compliance brings benefit,
and defiance brings harm,
the world will invariably obey -
this is顺应.
Issuing commands that are implemented and prohibitions that are observed
relies on the multitude for power.
Righteousness
cannot completely benefit all people under heaven,
yet benefit one person and the world follows;
tyranny
cannot completely harm all within the seas,
yet harm one person and the world rebels.
Therefore, in establishing or abolishing measures,
one cannot but be careful."
Lǎozǐ said:
"Bending an inch to stretch a foot,
accepting small wrongs for great righteousness,
the sage does this.
Nowadays, when rulers evaluate ministers,
they disregard their great achievements,
ignore their main conduct,
and seek their minor virtues,
thus losing the way to find worthies.
Therefore, when a person has substantial virtue,
do not inquire into their minor points;
when a person has great reputation,
do not pick at their small faults.
Human nature inevitably has shortcomings,
but if their main strategy is correct,
even with minor faults,
these should not burden them;
if their main strategy is wrong,
even exemplary village conduct
is not praiseworthy.
Thus those overly cautious in small matters achieve no success,
those who pick at conduct cannot accommodate the multitude.
Large things have sparse joints,
great measures have far-reaching fame -
this is the way to evaluate ministers."
Lǎozǐ said:
"From ancient times to the present,
none have been able to maintain perfect conduct.
Therefore, the gentleman does not demand completeness from anyone.
'Square but not cutting,
sharp-edged but not piercing,
straight but not unrestrained,'
broad and penetrating but not critical.
In moral virtue, civil and military arts,
do not demand complete human capability.
Cultivate oneself with the Way,
and do not make demands on others.
Easy to satisfy,
cultivating oneself with the Way,
then there will be no fault.
The jade tablet of the Xiàhòu shì
cannot be without flaws,
the bright moon pearl
cannot be without blemishes,
yet the world treasures them
because small defects do not obstruct great beauty.
Now if we record people's shortcomings
and forget their strengths,
yet wish to seek worthies in the world,
it will be difficult indeed.
The common view
sees low position and humble status,
dirty and disgraceful tasks,
without understanding their main strategy.
Therefore, the way to evaluate people is:
when noble, observe whom they recommend;
when wealthy, observe whom they give to;
when poor, observe what they won't accept;
when humble, observe what they won't do;
observe what difficulties they face
to know their courage;
move them with joy
to observe their character;
entrust them with wealth
to observe their benevolence;
startle them with fear
to observe their integrity;
like this,
then human nature can be known."
Lǎozǐ said:
Bending is the means by which one seeks to stretch out;
crookedness is the means by which one seeks straightness.
Bending an inch to stretch a foot,
accepting small crookedness for great straightness—
this is what the noble person does.
All rivers flow together,
but those that do not reach the sea are not considered valleys;
people pursue different paths,
but those who do not return to goodness are not considered noble persons.
Good words are valued for their feasibility,
good deeds are valued for their benevolence and righteousness.
The errors of a noble person
are like eclipses of the sun and moon—
they do not harm the light.
Thus, the wise do not act recklessly,
the brave do not kill indiscriminately;
they choose what is right to act upon,
and consider propriety in their conduct.
Therefore, their endeavors succeed and their achievements are reliable;
after death, their names are worthy of praise.
Even with wisdom and ability,
one must take benevolence and righteousness as the foundation to establish oneself.
Wisdom and ability are exercised together,
but the sage uniformly uses benevolence and righteousness as the standard.
Those who meet this standard are called noble persons;
those who do not are called petty persons.
Though a noble person may die,
their name does not perish;
though a petty person may gain power,
their crimes are not forgiven.
To hold the map of the world in the left hand
and cut one's throat with the right—
even a fool would not do this,
for the body is more precious than the world.
Yet those who die for the calamities of their ruler or parents
regard death as returning home—
righteousness is heavier than the body.
Thus, the greatest benefits of the world
are small compared to the body;
the body is what is valued,
but it is light compared to benevolence and righteousness.
This is what it means to take benevolence and righteousness as the standard.
Lǎozǐ said:
The principles of the Dào and virtue are like the sun and moon;
even the Yí Dí and Mán Mò cannot change their essence.
When choices align, praise or blame lie with customs;
when intentions and actions are uniform, poverty or success depend on the times.
Affairs that suit the age achieve success;
efforts that match the times gain fame.
Thus, those who establish merit and fame
are simple in their dealings with the world and cautious about timing.
When the moment arrives,
it is as brief as a breath.
In ancient times, those who used military force
did not covet land or treasure,
but aimed to preserve the perishing, quell chaos, and rid the people of harm.
Greedy and desire-ridden individuals
plunder the world,
causing the masses to stir,
with no place of peace.
Then a sage rises in fury,
to punish the violent,
pacify the chaotic age,
and eliminate harm for the world,
turning turbidity into clarity,
danger into peace—
thus, they cannot but intervene decisively.
The Chìdì caused fire disasters,
so Huángdì captured him;
Gònggōng brought flood harm,
so Zhuānxū executed him.
When teaching with the Dào
and guiding with virtue fail to persuade,
then impose authority and might;
if that does not secure compliance,
then restrain with weapons and armor.
Killing innocent people
to sustain an unrighteous ruler—
no harm is greater than this;
exhausting the world's wealth
to satisfy one person's desires—
no disaster is deeper than this;
indulging one person's desires
and increasing the world's calamities—
this is not accepted by the principles of heaven.
The reason for establishing a ruler
is to prohibit violence and chaos;
yet now, using the strength of the masses,
they instead become plunderers—
this is like adding wings to a tiger;
why not remove them?
Those who raise fish
must remove the otters;
those who rear birds and beasts
must eliminate the wolves;
how much more so for shepherding the people!
This is why weapons and armor arise.
Lǎozǐ said:
The way to govern a state
is to have no harsh decrees from above,
no burdensome administration by officials,
no deceitful conduct among scholars,
no excessive craftsmanship among artisans.
Affairs are handled without disruption,
and tools are complete without ornamentation.
A chaotic age is not so:
those who act strive to outdo each other in height,
those who practice rites boast with falseness;
carriages are极致ly carved,
utensils are excessively engraved;
those seeking goods compete for hard-to-obtain items as treasures,
those writing documents chase complexity and confusion as urgency;
matters involve deceitful arguments,
long delayed without resolution,
offering no benefit to order
but aiding chaos;
artisans create strange devices,
taking years to complete,
yet impractical for use.
The law of Shénnóng states:
If strong men do not plow,
some in the world will suffer hunger;
if women in their prime do not weave,
some in the world will suffer cold.
Thus, he personally plowed,
and his wife personally wove,
to set an example for the world.
In guiding the people,
he "did not value hard-to-obtain goods,"
nor esteem useless objects.
Therefore, if plowers do not work hard,
they have nothing to sustain life;
if weavers do not exert effort,
they have nothing to clothe themselves;
surplus and deficiency
fall upon each individual.
When food and clothing are abundant,
deceit and evil do not arise;
when there is peace and joy without trouble,
the world is harmonious.
The wise have no need to apply their strategies,
the brave have no need to exert their might.
Lǎo zǐ said:
The way of the hegemon and king,
is planned with strategy,
and mapped with schemes,
acting while upholding righteousness,
not for the purpose of seeking survival,
but rather to preserve what is perishing.
Therefore, upon hearing that the ruler of an enemy state
is tyrannizing his people,
immediately raise troops and approach his borders,
charging him with unrighteousness,
and criticizing his transgressions.
When the army reaches his outskirts,
command the generals:
Do not cut down trees,
do not dig up graves,
do not destroy the five grains,
do not burn stockpiles,
do not capture civilians as prisoners,
do not round up the six domestic animals;
then issue the decree:
The ruler of this state,
defies heaven and earth,
insults ghosts and spirits,
adjudicates lawsuits unjustly,
slaughters the innocent,
he is whom heaven punishes,
and the people仇视;
the coming of the army
is to abolish unrighteousness and bestow its virtue upon them,
any who dare oppose the way of heaven,
and disrupt the people as thieves,
shall face personal death and clan extinction,
those who follow with their household shall be rewarded with their household,
those who follow with their village shall be rewarded with their village,
those who follow with their township shall be enfeoffed with their township.
Conquer the state without harming its people,
depose its ruler,
change its governance,
honor its outstanding scholars,
promote its virtuous and good,
relieve its orphans and widows,
pity its poor and needy,
release those from prison,
reward those with merit,
the common people will open their doors to welcome them,
rinse rice and store it for them,
only worrying that they might not come.
Righteous armies arriving at the border,
cease without fighting,
unrighteous armies,
lead to corpses lying and blood flowing,
clashing with each other.
Therefore, those who fight for land
cannot achieve kingship,
those who seek for themselves,
cannot establish their merit,
those who act for others,
receive the help of the masses,
those who act for themselves,
are abandoned by the masses,
those helped by the masses,
though weak will surely become strong,
those abandoned by the masses,
though great will surely perish.
Lǎo zǐ said:
The highest righteousness,
governs the state and family,
administers within the borders,
practices benevolence and righteousness,
spreads virtue and bestows kindness,
establishes just laws,
blocks wicked paths,
ministers become close and attached,
the common people are harmonious and united,
superiors and inferiors are of one mind,
ministers unite in strength,
feudal lords submit to its authority,
all directions cherish its virtue,
cultivating governance in the court,
repelling enemies a thousand miles away,
issuing commands and orders with the world responding,
this is the highest level.
With vast land and numerous people,
wise rulers and excellent generals,
rich state and strong army,
discipline trustworthy,
orders clear,
when two enemies face each other,
before weapons clash,
the enemy flees and scatters,
this is the next level.
Knowing the suitability of the land,
familiar with the advantages of narrow passes,
understanding the changes of orthodox and unorthodox tactics,
observing the matters of formations,
when blades meet,
and arrows fly,
carrying the dead and aiding the wounded,
blood flowing for miles,
exposed bones filling the fields,
this is the lower level of righteousness.
The victory or defeat in war lies in governance,
if governance prevails over the people,
inferiors attach to their superiors,
then the army is strong,
if the people prevail over governance,
inferiors rebel against their superiors,
then the army is weak.
Thus, virtue and righteousness are sufficient to win the hearts of the world's people,
achievements are sufficient to meet the world's emergencies,
selections are sufficient to gain the hearts of worthy scholars,
planning is sufficient to decide the balance of priorities,
this is the way of the highest righteousness.
Lǎo zǐ said:
The reason a state is strong is due to its willingness to die,
the reason for willingness to die is righteousness,
the reason righteousness is practiced is authority,
therefore, command them with civility,
and unify them with martial means,
this is called certain victory;
authority and righteousness practiced together,
this is called certain strength.
When blades clash,
arrows and stones fall like rain,
and soldiers strive to be first,
it is because rewards are trustworthy and punishments are clear.
If the superior regards the inferior as sons,
the inferior will serve the superior as fathers,
if the superior regards the inferior as younger brothers,
the inferior will serve the superior as elder brothers,
if the superior regards the inferior as sons,
he will surely rule the four seas,
if the inferior regards the superior as fathers,
he will surely rectify the world,
if the superior regards the inferior as younger brothers,
then they will not find it hard to die for him,
if the inferior serve the superior as elder brothers,
then they will not find it hard to perish for him,
thus, enemies who are like fathers, sons, brothers,
cannot be fought against.
Therefore, a righteous ruler internally cultivates his governance,
to accumulate his virtue,
externally blocks evil,
to clarify his power,
observes their toil and rest,
to know their hunger and fullness,
when the battle day is set,
they will look upon death as returning home,
such is the effect of kindness bestowed.
Lǎozi said:
The True Men of high antiquity,
breathed in harmony with Yīn and Yáng,
and all living beings looked up to their virtue and lived in harmony and compliance.
At that time,
everything was governed by principle,
the hidden and subtle naturally took form,
pure simplicity had not yet dissipated,
and all things were greatly abundant.
When the world declined,
reaching the time of Fúxīshì,
people were dim and confused,
all wishing to depart from their childlike innocence,
and become awakened between heaven and earth,
their virtue became troubled and no longer unified.
By the time of Shénnóng
and Huángdì,
they governed the world strictly,
regulated the four seasons,
and harmonized Yīn and Yáng,
whereupon the myriad people all stood in awe and pondered,
listening intently and watching carefully,
so there was governance but no harmony.
Descending to the ages of Xià
and Yīn,
desires became linked to material things,
cleverness was seduced by external temptations,
and the nature and life lost their authenticity.
Extending to the Zhōu dynasty,
purity was diluted and simplicity scattered,
they departed from the Dào and engaged in artifice,
perverted virtue into conduct,
knowledge and cunning sprouted,
they used contrived learning to imitate the sages,
employed flowery and exaggerated speech to intimidate the masses,
polished and adorned the Shī and Shū,
to trade for fame and reputation,
each wishing to exercise their cunning and falsehood,
to be accepted in the world,
thus losing the root of the great ancestor,
so the world suffered the loss of nature and life,
the decline had been gradually accumulating for a long time.
Therefore, the learning of the ultimate person
aims to return nature to nothingness,
and let the mind wander in emptiness;
the learning of the世俗
flaunts virtue and plunders nature,
internally distressing the five viscera,
acting violently and exceeding knowledge,
to clamor for reputation in the world,
this is what the ultimate person does not do.
Flaunting virtue is self-display,
plundering nature severs life,
as for the ultimate person, they are settled in the realm of life and death,
understand the principle of honor and disgrace,
the whole world praising them does not encourage them more,
the whole world criticizing them does not discourage them more,
they have grasped the essence of the ultimate Dào.
Lǎozi said:
In ancient times, people wore their hair loose and had no rolled collars,
yet they ruled the world,
their virtue gave life and did not kill,
gave and did not take away,
the world did not criticize their clothing,
all embraced their virtue;
at that time,
Yīn and Yáng were harmonious and peaceful,
all things multiplied and thrived,
the nests of flying birds
could be reached down and explored,
running beasts could be tethered and followed.
When it declined,
birds, beasts, insects, and snakes
all became harmful to humans,
so they cast iron and forged blades,
to defend against these difficulties,
when people are pressed by difficulties they seek convenience,
facing calamities they create preparations,
each using their wisdom,
to remove what harms them,
and pursue what benefits them,
old ways cannot be followed blindly,
tools and instruments cannot be fixed,
thus the laws and measures of the former kings
are subject to change,
hence it is said
"The name that can be named
is not the eternal name."
The Five Emperors had different ways but their virtue covered the world,
the Three Kings had different deeds but their names were established for posterity,
this is adapting to the times.
Just as Shī Kuáng's tuning of the five notes,
the shifts up and down are not constant,
yet measured by inches and feet,
none miss the mark,
so one who understands the essence of music can compose,
words have a root master within,
and one who knows the use of compass, square, hook, and line can govern people,
thus the institutions of the former kings,
if unsuitable, should be discarded,
and the affairs of later ages,
if good, should be adopted.
Therefore, the sages who created rites and music
were not constrained by rites and music,
those who regulate things
are not constrained by things,
those who establish laws
are not constrained by laws,
hence it is said
"The Dào that can be spoken
is not the eternal Dào."
Lǎozi said:
In the past, the sage kings
looked up and took images from heaven,
looked down and took measures from earth,
in the middle took models from humans,
harmonized the Qì of Yīn and Yáng,
balanced the nodes of the four seasons,
observed the suitability of hills, plains, waters, marshes, fertility, aridity, heights, and lows,
to establish affairs and generate wealth,
eliminate the troubles of hunger and cold,
ward off the disasters of illness and disease,
centrally received human affairs,
to institute rites and music,
practice the way of benevolence and righteousness,
to govern human relationships.
They classified the natures of metal, wood, water, fire, and earth,
to establish the closeness of father and son and form families;
listened to the numbers of the five notes' clarity and turbidity and the six pitch-pipes' mutual generation,
to establish the righteousness of ruler and minister and form states;
observed the sequence of the four seasons' first, middle, and last months,
to establish the order of elder and younger and form offices;
divided the land into regions,
assigned duties to govern them,
established great schools to educate,
this is the guiding principle of governance.
Those who attained the Dào were elevated,
those who lost the Dào were discarded.
Things never stretch without relaxing,
succeed without failing,
only the sage can achieve without decline.
When the sages first created music,
it was to return to the spirit and prevent excess,
revert to the heavenly heart;
when it declined,
it flowed without return,
became excessive and fond of sensuality, , ,
leading to the loss of states;
when they created writing,
it was to manage all affairs,
so the foolish would not forget,
the wise could record events,
when it declined,
it was used for deceit to exonerate the guilty,
and kill the innocent.
When they created parks,
it was to supply the needs of the ancestral temples,
and train soldiers to prepare for emergencies;
when it declined,
it became racing, shooting, and hunting that robbed people of their time,
and exhausted their strength.
When they esteemed the worthy,
it was to balance education and transformation,
rectify legal cases and disputes,
with the worthy in position,
the capable in office,
benefits extended below,
the myriad people cherished their virtue;
when it declined,
factions formed and colluded,
each promoting their associates,
abandoning public good for private gain,
inside and outside mutually elevating,
with wicked people in position,
and the worthy living in seclusion.
The way of heaven and earth is such that
when something reaches its extreme, it reverses;
when it is full, it diminishes.
Thus, the sage governs by addressing flaws and reforming institutions,
changing methods when tasks are completed.
Its beauty lies in harmony,
and its failure lies in the abuse of power.
The way of the sage states:
Without cultivating ritual and righteousness,
integrity and shame cannot be established.
If the people lack integrity and shame,
they cannot be governed.
Without understanding ritual and righteousness,
laws cannot correct them.
Without exalting goodness and abolishing ugliness,
people will not aspire to ritual and righteousness.
Without laws, governance is impossible;
without understanding ritual and righteousness,
laws cannot be implemented.
Laws can execute the unfilial,
but they cannot make people filial;
they can punish thieves,
but they cannot make people honest.
When a sage king reigns above,
he clarifies likes and dislikes to guide the people,
regulates praise and blame to lead them,
draws close to the worthy and promotes them,
disdains the unworthy and dismisses them,
so punishments are set aside and not used,
and ritual and righteousness are cultivated, with virtue and worthiness entrusted.
Thus, the most elevated in the world
are made the Three Dukes,
the most elevated in a region
are made the Nine Ministers,
the most elevated in a state
are made the twenty-seven Great Officers,
the most elevated in a district
are made the eighty-one Exemplary Scholars.
Those whose wisdom surpasses ten thousand are called yīng (heroes),
those surpassing a thousand are called jùn (talented),
those surpassing a hundred are called jié (outstanding),
and those surpassing ten are called háo (prominent).
One who understands the way of heaven and earth,
comprehends the principles of human emotions,
is magnanimous enough to embrace the multitude,
benevolent enough to win over distant lands,
and wise enough to understand expediency,
is a yīng among people.
One whose virtue is sufficient to educate and transform,
whose conduct is sufficient to uphold righteousness,
whose trustworthiness is sufficient to gain followers,
and whose clarity is sufficient to illuminate those below,
is a jùn among people.
One whose actions can serve as a model,
whose wisdom is sufficient to resolve doubts,
whose trustworthiness can uphold agreements,
whose integrity can manage the division of wealth,
whose deeds can be emulated,
and whose words can be followed,
is a jié among people.
One who坚守职责不废弛,
adheres to righteousness without bias,
faces difficulties without seeking escape,
and encounters gains without coveting them,
is a háo among people.
Yīng, jùn, háo, and jié,
each according to their capacity, occupy their positions,
flowing from the root to the branches,
controlling the light with the heavy,
with those above leading and those below harmonizing,
so within the four seas,
all hearts unite in one purpose,
turning away from greed and baseness,
and aspiring to benevolence and righteousness.
In transforming the people,
it is like the wind bending the grass.
If the unworthy are set over the worthy,
even severe punishments cannot prevent treachery.
The small cannot control the large,
the weak cannot command the strong—
such is the nature of heaven and earth.
Thus, the sage promotes the worthy to achieve merit,
while the unworthy ruler promotes those like himself.
Observing whom they promote,
order and chaos are distinguished;
examining their factions,
the worthy and unworthy can be discerned.
Lǎo zǐ said:
Those who practice ritual
carve and polish human nature,
distort and oppose its true feelings.
Though the eyes desire, they are restrained by rules;
though the heart delights, it is moderated by ritual.
Hastening and circling about,
bowing and kneeling humbly,
with meat congealed and uneaten,
wine settled and undrunk,
externally binding their forms,
internally distressing their minds,
they clamp the harmony of yīn and yáng and oppress the true nature of life,
thus remaining sorrowful throughout their lives.
Why is this?
They do not address the root of desires,
but forbid the desires themselves;
they do not trace the source of joy,
but block the joy itself.
This is like not mending the pen of a captive beast
yet forbidding its wild heart,
or trying to stop the flow of a river with one's hands.
Therefore it is said:
"Open the floodgates,
and complete affairs,
and one will be beyond rescue for life."
Ritual
suppresses emotions and blocks desires,
using righteousness for self-defense.
Though the heart feels stifled and choked,
the body and nature starve and thirst,
one forces oneself out of necessity,
thus unable to live out their natural lifespan.
Ritual
cannot make people have no desires,
but can only stop them;
music
cannot make people have no joys,
but can only prevent them.
Making the world fear punishment and dare not steal
is not as good as ensuring they have no desire to steal!
Thus, knowing something is useless,
even the greedy will decline it;
not knowing it is useless,
even the honest cannot yield it.
Those who lose their states,
perish by others' hands,
and are laughed at by the world—
it is always due to desires.
Knowing that a fan in winter
or a fur coat in summer
are useless to oneself,
then all things turn to dust and dirt!
Thus, to stop boiling by scooping out the water
only makes it boil more fiercely;
knowing the root cause,
one simply removes the fire.
Lǎo zǐ said:
Following one's nature is called the Dào;
attaining one's innate nature is called dé.
When nature is lost, then benevolence is valued;
when the Dào is lost, then righteousness is valued.
With benevolence and righteousness established, the Dào and dé are abandoned;
with simplicity dispersed, ritual and music are adorned.
When right and wrong appear, the people are confused;
when pearls and jade are prized, the world contends.
Ritual
is used to distinguish the noble from the base, the honored from the humble;
righteousness
is used to harmonize the relationships between ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger brother, husband and wife.
In decadent times, ritual
involves reverence in interactions.
Those who practice righteousness
give alms to gain favor.
Ruler and minister blame each other,
and flesh and blood breed resentment.
Thus, where water accumulates, cannibalistic insects arise;
where earth accumulates, flesh-eating beasts appear;
where ritual and music are adorned, deceit and hypocrisy are born.
In decadent times, governance
does not accumulate means for nurturing life,
but dilutes the purity of the world,
scatters the simplicity of the world,
confuses the myriad people,
turning clarity into turbidity,
so lives drift aimlessly,
all in chaos and striving,
with integrity and trustworthiness decaying,
and people losing their innate nature.
Laws conflict with righteousness,
conduct contradicts benefit,
rich and poor oppress each other,
and the difference between ruler and servant
is not worth discussing.
Where there is surplus, there is yielding;
where there is lack, there is contention.
Yielding gives rise to ritual and righteousness;
contention gives rise to violence and chaos.
Thus, with many desires, affairs are not simplified;
with endless demands, strife does not cease.
Therefore, in an orderly age, even the petty uphold correctness,
and profit cannot tempt them;
in a chaotic age, even the noble commit treachery,
and laws cannot restrain them.
Lǎozǐ said:
The rulers of a declining age
bore into mountains and rocks,
hoard gold and jade,
gather clams and mollusks,
smelt bronze and iron,
yet the myriad things do not flourish;
they cut open wombs and burn the countryside,
overturn nests and destroy eggs,
so the phoenix does not soar,
the qílín does not roam,
they construct wooden towers,
set forests ablaze for hunting,
drain ponds to fish,
pile earth to dwell on hills,
dig the ground to drink from wells,
dredge rivers to make pools,
build walls for fortification,
capture beasts to domesticate them;
then yīn and yáng become disordered,
the four seasons lose their sequence,
thunderbolts cause destruction,
hail and frost bring harm,
the myriad things wither and die young,
with more than half perishing,
grass and trees wither in summer,
the three rivers cease to flow.
They divide mountains, streams, and valleys,
establishing territorial boundaries,
count the population's numbers,
imposing quotas and divisions,
set up mechanisms and barriers for defense,
regulate ceremonial colors,
distinguish noble from base,
differentiate the worthy from the unworthy,
implement rewards and punishments;
then arms and armor arise and contentious strife is born,
cruel killing of the innocent,
punishing the guiltless,
thus emerges.
Lǎozǐ said:
When the world is about to lose its inherent nature,
it is like the rising of yīn energy,
the ruler is benighted and unenlightened,
the Dào is abandoned and not practiced,
virtue is extinguished and not promoted,
undertakings contradict heaven,
issuing commands contrary to the four seasons,
spring and autumn withhold their harmony,
heaven and earth withdraw their virtue;
the ruler occupies the throne uneasily,
high officials retreat into seclusion and do not speak,
ministers conform to the ruler's wishes and seek favor,
estrange bone relatives to save themselves,
wicked men flatter and scheme in secret,
hastily supporting arrogant rulers and mirroring their desires,
creating chaos to achieve their aims;
therefore ministers are at odds and not close,
bone relatives are estranged and not attached,
fields have no standing sprouts,
roads see no leisurely steps,
accumulated gold breaks its purity,
jade discs show no surplus,
tortoise shells have no belly markings,
divination with yarrow stalks is daily performed,
the world does not unite as one family,
feudal lords make laws with different customs.
They uproot and discard the foundation,
carve out the five punishments,
engage in harsh governance,
contend over trifles like knife tips,
slaughter the common people,
exterminating more than half,
raise armies to cause trouble,
attack cities and kill indiscriminately,
overthrow the high and endanger the secure,
large assault chariots,
tall multiple ramparts,
deploy combat formations,
make battle lines on deadly paths,
confront formidable enemies,
the common people revolt at once,
if reputation is temporarily flourishing,
annexing states and acquiring land,
corpses lie in tens of thousands,
the old, weak, hungry, and cold who die,
are beyond counting.
From this time onward,
the world has never been able to secure its inherent nature,
or enjoy its customs.
Sages and worthies vigorously arise,
holding fast to the Dào and virtue,
assisting with benevolence and righteousness,
those nearby offer their wisdom,
those afar are drawn by their virtue,
the world blends into one,
children and grandchildren succeed each other,
assistants are capable;
they dismiss slanderous and flattering tendencies,
cease sophistical debates,
abolish harsh laws,
remove burdensome and oppressive matters,
block the traces of rumors,
close the door to factionalism,
diminish cleverness and ability,
follow the great constant,
disregard the limbs,
set aside keen senses,
greatly penetrate the primordial chaos,
the myriad things each return to their root.
Now, the sage cannot create the time,
but when the time comes, he does not miss it,
thus it does not get cut off midway.
Lǎozǐ said:
The Fēng River's depth of ten fathoms does not accept dust and dirt,
with metal and iron inside,
their forms visible from outside,
not because it is not deep and clear,
but fish, turtles, jiāo, and dragons do not return to it.
On stone, the five grains do not grow,
on bald mountains, elk and deer do not roam,
for there is no shelter or shade.
Thus, governing with harshness as discernment,
with severity as clarity,
with oppressing subordinates as loyalty,
with numerous schemes as achievement,
such approaches,
are like stretching leather,
the larger it gets,
the more it tends to tear,
"When governance is unobtrusive,
the people are genuine;
when governance is scrutinizing,
the people are cunning."
Lǎozǐ said:
"Govern the state with correctness,
use the military with surprise."
First establish an invincible governance,
then seek victory over the enemy,
to attack others' chaos with one's own disorder,
is like responding to fire with fire,
to water with water.
Sameness is insufficient to govern each other,
thus difference is used for surprise.
Stillness is the surprise to agitation,
order to chaos,
satiety to hunger,
ease to toil.
The interaction of surprise and correctness,
is like water, fire, metal, and wood replacing one another,
ensuring victory wherever applied.
Thus, with equal virtue, the numerous overcome the few;
with equal strength, the wise control the foolish;
with equal wisdom, the strategic capture the unstrategic.
